hypothesis: Because scoring only compares items inside one user, the only features that can move the metric are item-side ones that vary across a user's candidates, and the organisers' one-at-a-time sweep tested each such feature alone against a five-field FM that already encodes item identity — so each individual item-side rate looked redundant with `video_id`'s embedding. I claim the three item-side historical signals are complementary rather than redundant with each other because they encode different mechanisms: `video_long_view_rate_decayed` (recency-weighted item propensity, robust to popularity drift), `video_completion_ratio_hist` (engagement depth independent of impression count), and `long_view_rate_by_duration_group` (the duration confound that makes long-view mechanically easier for short videos, which `dur_bucket` only captures as a coarse identity term). Added together on top of all five official fields with FM k=16, lr=0.001 held identical to n003, I predict full-tier primary >= 0.6036 (>= +0.002 over 0.6016), with the gain concentrated in the pop_q1/pop_q2 segments where n003 is weakest (0.4408/0.4836) because cold items have uninformative `video_id` embeddings and must be ranked from aggregate history, and near-zero change in pop_q4. If the combination lands inside noise of 0.6016, then item-side history is genuinely subsumed by the item-identity embedding at full fidelity and the entire feature drawer is closed, redirecting the remaining iterations to loss form (screen ablation's +0.0017 for pairwise) and ensembling. [ref: D2Q \u2014 Zhan et al., KDD 2022]
